page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-64 is a flexible compute instance configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 64.0 GB of memory. Driven by an AMD EPYC 9J14 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz with dedicated CPU allocation, the architecture provides two threads per physical core and maintains an expanded memory profile of 8 GB per vCPU.

The instance contains no integrated local NVMe storage and includes zero GPU accelerators, requiring persistence to be managed via external network-attached block volumes. Network connectivity is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The underlying hardware relies on dedicated AMD EPYC processor allocation without burstable core sharing, yielding stable multi-threaded execution.

With an elevated 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-64 achieves strong qualitative memory density without obligating instances to high compute core footprints. This hardware resource balance is well-suited for memory-sensitive environments such as medium-scale in-memory databases, Redis caches, data transformation jobs, and general enterprise application hosting.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-64 is an x86_64 compute instance configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. Paired with 64.0 GB of memory, the server maintains an elevated 1:8 compute-to-RAM ratio providing 8 GB per vCPU. The instance is provisioned without local storage disks or GPU hardware acceleration, requiring remote storage volumes for persistent data, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute execution, while the generous memory footprint delivers efficient resource density for memory-bound tasks without requiring excess compute provisioning. This configuration is aligned with in-memory caching, relational database workloads, background processing pipelines, and general business applications.
